page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per thread. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Network and storage persistence rely entirely on remote managed disks via Azure Premium Storage capabilities, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Benchmark assessments position the server in the middle performance quartile across general computing tasks. It achieved a Geekbench score of 1,660.0 in single-core and 6,201.0 in multi-core evaluations, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11,502.33. Memory bandwidth reaches 419.81 GB/sec on cached 16 KB blocks and 59.21 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads. In-memory data structures perform reliably, demonstrated by 8.02 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavily parallelized compute tasks show constraints, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression landing in the lower 25% of tested systems.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the constrained core count paired with large RAM limits licensing costs for software priced per core while maintaining sufficient memory footprints. Due to the high memory density and absence of local storage, the instance fits in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, Redis deployments, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads requiring a restrained core count. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 48 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU, while omitting bundled local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance, producing a multi-core Geekbench score of 6,201.0, a PassMark memory score of 2,709.75, and 8.02 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the 8-vCPU ceiling on parallel compression routines and larger model inference. With its high memory-to-core density, this configuration is well matched for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, and enterprise transactional systems.
